dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (USONA Institute Investigational Drug Supply Program; Lot# AMS0167) was dissolved in saline and administered at a dose of 1.5 mg/kg... All drugs were administered intraperitoneally at a 1.0 ml/kg injection volume

Merged candidate 'Between-session reversal learning' / 'Home-cage operant reversal learning' / 'Reversal Learning (operant)' into one Reversal Learning assay (same FED3 paradigm, includes 5-HT1A/5-HT2A antagonist arms which per rubric are still one assay).
Merged FR-extinction and VR-extinction into one Extinction assay (same FED3 paradigm, same outcome of response suppression with no rewards).
Merged classic PR and re-setting PR into one Progressive Ratio assay (same apparatus, same effortful-responding construct measured by breakpoint/engagement).
Kept Variable Ratio schedule training as a separate assay from Extinction because the recording measures response vigor under uncertainty rather than extinction.

ABA: scored E1=Home cage (transparent living chamber = home cage used as the testing environment), E5=Yes (running wheel as enrichment object in the test cage), D1=Continuous monitoring and D2=>6 h (wheel running is recorded continuously by Scurry software across the 10-day period), D6=Yes (continuous recording spans >=6 h).

FED3 home-cage operant tasks: E5 scored No because the FED3 device IS the test apparatus rather than added enrichment; food_restriction='no' because chow was ad libitum in the home cage during testing.

assays.assay_description: Rats individually housed in transparent chambers with a running wheel and removable food basket; 7-day baseline wheel habituation followed by up to 10 days of 90 min/day food access. Body weight, wheel revolutions, food anticipatory activity, and food intake recorded continuously. Psilocybin administered 24 h before ABA onset.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered intraperitoneally at a 1.0 ml/kg injection volume

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were allowed to habituate to the wheel for seven days to determine baseline running wheel activity (RWA)

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were individually housed in transparent living chambers with a removable food basket and a running wheel

food_restriction.evidence: During the ABA period, food access was restricted to 90 min/day at the onset of the dark phase (1100-1230 h)

water_restriction.evidence: Water access during ABA chambers not restricted (ad libitum housing standard); not explicitly restricted in methods.

time_to_assay.evidence: psilocybin was administered 24 h prior to the onset of timed food restriction

sample_size.evidence: Weight loss trajectories of individual rats (n = 16 saline; n = 19 psilocybin)

outcomes.summary: A single dose of psilocybin (1.5 mg/kg, i.p.) administered 24 h before ABA onset improved body weight maintenance: psilocybin-treated rats spent more days above 85% baseline body weight and were protected from severe weight loss. There were no overall effects on wheel running or food intake, but ABA-resistant psilocybin rats showed reduced compulsive running and increased food anticipatory activity and intake.
outcomes.statistics: Days >85% BW: t(33)=2.508, p=0.0172; severe weight loss: t(33)=2.146, p=0.0394; daily % BW loss trend: t(33)=1.918, p=0.0638; wheel revolutions Treatment F(1,33)=1.159, p=0.2985; ABA Phase F(1,33)=126.5, p<0.0001
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin-treated rats spent significantly more days above 85% of their baseline body weight (p = 0.0172)... psilocybin prevented severe weight loss associated with ABA (p = 0.0394).

B1_num_measures.evidence: body weight, % days >85% BW, daily weight loss, severe weight loss proportion, total wheel revolutions, food anticipatory activity (FAA), daily food intake, mean intake

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Daily totals reported across the 10-day period; no within-session minute-by-minute analysis.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Measures are wheel running, food intake, and body weight; not scored ethological acts.

B6_cognitive.evidence: ABA outcomes assess physiological adaptation/weight loss, not a learning task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Running activity was recorded by the Scurry Activity Wheel Software (beam-break/position).

E1_environment_type.evidence: rats were individually housed in transparent living chambers with a removable food basket and a running wheel

E2_shelter.evidence: Transparent living chamber; no enclosed refuge described.

E3_bedding.evidence: Bedding not described in the ABA chamber.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Running wheel present in the home cage during the recording period.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single chamber containing a food basket and wheel; not physically partitioned compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were individually housed during ABA.

E8_food_water.evidence: Food access (90 min/day) and water provided in the testing cage during the continuous recording period.

D1_continuity.evidence: Running activity was recorded by the Scurry Activity Wheel Software... persisted for a maximum of 10 days

D2_session_duration.evidence: Continuous wheel monitoring across each 24 h day during baseline and the 10-day ABA period.

D3_recording_days.evidence: 7-day baseline habituation + up to 10-day ABA = up to 17 recording days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Rats were allowed to habituate to the wheel for seven days to determine baseline running wheel activity

D5_followup.evidence: Behaviour recorded for up to 10 days after single psilocybin dose.

D6_circadian.evidence: Continuous 24 h wheel recording each day spans >=6 h.

assays.assay_description: Home-cage FED3 device with two nose-poke ports and pellet magazine. After FR1/FR3/FR5 training, reward contingencies reversed 18 h after saline/psilocybin (with or without ketanserin, MDL100907 or WAY100635 pretreatment). 3 h daily sessions over up to 3 reversal days; accuracy, target/non-target pokes, latencies, rewards measured.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered intraperitoneally at a 1.0 ml/kg injection volume

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were habituated to sucrose pellet rewards for two days prior to training... magazine training on a 'free feeding' schedule

setup_restrain.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage; animals freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and standard laboratory chow (Barastoc, Australia) throughout

water_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water... throughout

time_to_assay.evidence: Psilocybin was administered 18 h prior to reversal of reward contingencies

sample_size.evidence: Saline+SAL n=15, MDL+SAL n=9, WAY+SAL n=13, Saline+PSI n=16, MDL+PSI n=9, WAY+PSI n=13 (from Fig. 3/4 reporting).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (18 h post-dose) improved reversal accuracy on the initial reversal day, primarily by reducing perseverative non-target pokes and shortening latencies to first poke and first reward. 5-HT2A antagonism (MDL100907) alone abolished reversal learning, but co-administration with psilocybin rescued performance. 5-HT1A antagonism (WAY100635) negated psilocybin's improvement, implicating 5-HT1AR in psilocybin's pro-flexibility action.
outcomes.statistics: Accuracy Treatment F(1,29)=5.128, p=0.0312; non-target pokes t(18)=2.425, p=0.0260; latency to first poke t(18)=2.307, p=0.0332; latency to first reward t(18)=2.291, p=0.0343; MDL+SAL vs SAL+SAL accuracy p=0.0221; WAY+PSI vs SAL+PSI accuracy p=0.0024; MDL+PSI vs MDL+SAL accuracy t(16)=3.034, p=0.0079
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin... produced an improvement in response accuracy (p = 0.0312)... specifically by reduced responding to the non-target (incorrect) port (p = 0.0260)... improvements in reversal accuracy and engagement were abolished when psilocybin was co-administered with the selective 5-HT1AR antagonist (WAY100635).

B1_num_measures.evidence: accuracy, criterion proportion, total pokes, target pokes, non-target pokes, rewards earned, latency to first poke, latency to first target poke, latency to first reward, session duration

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: first reversal session analysed in 6 x 30 min time bins (Fig. 2B)

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition/sequence analysis of pokes reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Operant nose-pokes are not ethological behaviours.

B5_social.evidence: Animal alone in home cage during testing.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Reversal learning task tests cognitive flexibility.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: FED3 uses infra-red beams to detect nose-pokes and pellet collection (beam-break, not behavioural classifier).

E1_environment_type.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage

E2_shelter.evidence: Tinted transparent cage; no shelter described.

E3_bedding.evidence: Bedding in testing cage not described.

E5_enrichment.evidence: FED3 is the test apparatus, not an enrichment object.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single home-cage space containing the FED3; not physically partitioned compartments.

E8_food_water.evidence: ad libitum access to water and standard laboratory chow throughout; sucrose pellets delivered during session.

D1_continuity.evidence: rats underwent 3 days of testing on the reversed FR5 schedule

D2_session_duration.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage for a 3 h session between 12:00-15:00

D3_recording_days.evidence: 3 days of testing on the reversed FR5 schedule

D4_baseline.evidence: Training data (FR1/3/5) precede drug but are not analysed as baseline reversal performance.

D5_followup.evidence: Recording started 18 h post-dose; no >=24 h follow-up reported for reversal accuracy beyond the 3-day window.

D6_circadian.evidence: 3 h session does not span >=6 h.

assays.assay_description: Following FR5 (or VR20) training, psilocybin or saline administered; over the next 2-3 days the FED3 was provided with no rewards. Number/pattern of nose-pokes across extinction sessions measured. Includes a 7-day post-treatment test of response suppression.

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were habituated to sucrose pellet rewards for two days prior to training

setup_restrain.evidence: Home-cage operant testing; animals freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and standard laboratory chow throughout

time_to_assay.evidence: saline or psilocybin was administered immediately following the final FR5 training session. Over the next 3 days rats underwent extinction testing... extinction following variable ratio training tested up to ~7 days post-dose.

sample_size.evidence: FR extinction Treatment F(1,17) implies ~19; VR extinction F(1,21) implies ~23.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no significant effect on extinction of FR-trained responding or on response suppression following VR training tested 7 days later.
outcomes.statistics: FR extinction Treatment F(1,17)=0.3212, p=0.5783; Interaction F(179,3043)=0.2623, p>0.9999; VR extinction Treatment F(1,21)=0.2681, p=0.6100
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin treatment had no effect on... the ability to extinguish a previously learned response (p = 0.5783)... no improvement in response suppression 7 days following psilocybin treatment (p = 0.6100).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total pokes and target-vs-non-target pokes across extinction sessions.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Within-session time course analysed (Interaction F(179,3043) over 179 time bins).

B6_cognitive.evidence: Extinction requires learning that responses no longer yield reward.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage

E8_food_water.evidence: ad libitum chow and water in the home cage throughout testing.

D1_continuity.evidence: Over the next 3 days rats underwent extinction testing... 2 consecutive days of extinction testing after VR.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage for a 3 h session; VR extinction had 24 h access to FED3 (with 3 h primary window).

D3_recording_days.evidence: 3 days FR extinction + 2 days VR extinction.

D5_followup.evidence: no improvement in response suppression 7 days following psilocybin treatment

assays.assay_description: Home-cage FED3 PR task with exponential schedule (5*e^(0.2n)-5) testing breakpoint; followed by an FR5 reinstatement session and a re-setting PR session in which the ratio reset to 1 after any 10 min of inactivity. Psilocybin administered 18 h before the first PR test.

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were habituated to sucrose pellet rewards for two days prior to training; FR1/3/5 training preceded PR.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and standard laboratory chow throughout

time_to_assay.evidence: saline or psilocybin was administered at completion of the final FR5 training session and the next day rats underwent a progressive ratio

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin did not change breakpoint on the classic PR task but selectively increased task engagement (target pokes) on the re-setting PR session, when effort cost was lowered by ratio resets. Effects emerged only after experience with the resetting reward economy.
outcomes.statistics: Classic PR breakpoint t(23)=0.7795, p=0.4436; R-PR target pokes p=0.0209; classic PR target pokes p>0.9999
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin treatment had no effect on breakpoint... (p = 0.4436)... psilocybin increased task engagement specifically during the R-PR session... increases in the number of target but not non-target pokes (R-PR p = 0.0209).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Breakpoint, target pokes, non-target pokes, pellets earned, engagement metrics across PR and R-PR.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: No within-session time-binned analysis reported for PR.

B6_cognitive.evidence: PR/R-PR task; in R-PR rats must learn the new reward economy.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage

E8_food_water.evidence: Ad libitum chow/water in home cage and sucrose pellets delivered during session.

D1_continuity.evidence: PR session, FR5 reinstatement session, and R-PR session run on successive days.

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowing animals access to the operant devices for 3 h using a standard PR schedule

D3_recording_days.evidence: PR + FR5 reinstatement + R-PR = ~3 recording days.

D5_followup.evidence: All PR/R-PR sessions within the first ~3 days post-dose; no >=24 h pure follow-up isolated.

assays.assay_description: Following FR1 training and psilocybin/saline administration, rats were trained on VR5, VR10, and VR20 schedules (2 days each) on FED3 to assess response vigor under increasing reinforcement uncertainty.

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were habituated to sucrose pellet rewards for two days prior to training; FR1 training preceded VR.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and standard laboratory chow throughout

time_to_assay.evidence: saline or psilocybin was administered. The following day rats were trained at variable ratio (VR) schedules of VR5, VR10 and VR20 (two days on each schedule)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no effect on response vigor or goal-directed engagement across increasingly uncertain VR schedules.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin treatment had no effect on... response vigour under uncertain (variable) schedules of reinforcement (p = 0.2013).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Target pokes, rewards earned across VR schedules.

B6_cognitive.evidence: VR schedules require learning under uncertainty.

E8_food_water.evidence: Ad libitum chow/water plus pellet rewards during session.

D1_continuity.evidence: two days on each schedule (VR5, VR10, VR20)

D2_session_duration.evidence: Operant testing was conducted once daily in the home cage for a 3 h session

D3_recording_days.evidence: 2 days on each of VR5, VR10, VR20 = 6 recording days.

D4_baseline.evidence: FR1 training is not analysed as a baseline of VR performance.

D5_followup.evidence: VR sessions extend up to ~7 days after the single dose.
